cases.name: LULAC v. Executive Office of the President (EO 14248 elections order)
cases.court: D.D.C. (Judge Colleen Kollar-Kotelly)
cases.stake: Challenge to Trump's March 2025 elections EO. Kollar-Kotelly permanently blocked the documentary proof-of-citizenship requirement for the federal form (Oct 2025) and, on Jan 30, 2026, permanently blocked agencies from assessing citizenship before giving voter forms to public-assistance enrollees and DoD from demanding proof from military voters: 'our Constitution does not allow the President to impose unilateral changes to federal election procedures.' White House said the ruling is 'not the final say.'

cases.name: United States v. California (26A624) — ~20,000 'noncitizen' mail ballots
cases.court: C.D. Cal. (Judge David O. Carter) → Ninth Circuit → Supreme Court
cases.stake: DOJ sought to force California to segregate ~20,000 mail ballots from voters it flagged as likely noncitizens (list conceded unreliable). Carter ruled for the state; the Ninth Circuit affirmed 2-1; SCOTUS denied relief within hours on Nov 2, 2026 with no noted dissents. Boasberg separately found the administration likely violated the Elections Clause but denied Democratic groups' TRO for standing.

cases.name: SEIU & NAACP v. DOJ/DHS (threats to prosecute election workers)
cases.court: N.D. Cal. (Judge Trina Thompson)
cases.stake: DOJ and DHS letters threatened to prosecute election officials who processed ballots of allegedly ineligible voters. Thompson's TRO (Oct 30, 2026) found likely violation of the VRA's anti-intimidation provision; bars threats and demands to purge, withhold, segregate or not count ballots; requires notice to letter recipients. Administration said it was 'evaluating all options' and reportedly appealed.

cases.name: Louisiana v. Callais
cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States (No. 24-109)
cases.stake: Not an administration-party case. 6-3 (Alito): VRA Section 2 did not require Louisiana's second majority-Black district, so the race-based map was an unconstitutional gerrymander; new, stricter Section 2 standards (alternative maps must satisfy nonracial goals; polarization analysis must control for party; focus on present-day intentional discrimination). Kagan dissent (Sotomayor, Jackson). Outcome favored GOP-led 2026 redistricting.

cases.name: Abbott v. LULAC (Texas 2025 congressional map)
cases.court: W.D. Tex. three-judge court → Supreme Court
cases.stake: Trump-backed mid-decade Texas map targeting five Democratic seats. Three-judge panel found a likely racial gerrymander (Nov 2025); SCOTUS stayed in Dec 2025 (Kagan dissenting) and summarily reversed in a one-paragraph order Apr 27, 2026 (three liberal justices dissenting). Map in use for the 2026 midterms.

cases.name: Tangipa v. Newsom (California Proposition 50 map; DOJ intervening)
cases.court: C.D. Cal. three-judge court → Supreme Court
cases.stake: California Republicans, joined by the Trump DOJ, challenged the voter-approved Prop 50 map (up to five Democratic pickups) as a racial gerrymander. Divided three-judge panel (Staton) upheld it as a political gerrymander (Jan 2026); SCOTUS declined to block it Feb 4, 2026 with no noted dissents. Map in use for 2026.
